entries.text: A reviewer (GPT-6.1-Sol) checked your 7 commits and verified the two findings below. Note: the checkout is now on branch docs/hosted-plan (one doc commit on top of yours). Create branch fix/site-review from feat/package-and-action (not from docs/hosted-plan) and fix both at the root cause, each with a test that reproduces the reviewer's input first (see it fail, then fix): - P1: redact all published metadata (both commit objects' subjects, thread titles, anything in LedgerRange that is free text) and remove the absolute repo path from the static page and job summary (use the repo's basename or the remote's owner/name). `ledger show` too. - P2: in static pages, render Markdown images as text links (no automatic load) and add a strict CSP meta (default-src 'none'; inline script/style only as the page needs; img-src data: only). Add a test that renders a page with ![x](https://attacker.example/...) in a message and asserts no external URL is loaded (no , CSP present). Consider whether the live viewer should also block remote images in Markdown; do it there too if cheap. Same verification and commit rules as before (no push). Server ports: use 4785 if you need one. Report commits and verification. Review findings: ── assistant · just now Two verified findings. - **P1: The published page bypasses redaction for commit subjects and repository paths.** See `src/server/Ledger.ts:699` and `src/core/ledgerSite.ts:14`. - A commit subject of `fix: API_TOKEN=[redacted] appears unchanged in `index.html` and the action’s job summary. A repo at `` also appears unchanged in the page’s JSON and summary. `ledger show` prints both at `src/server/ledgerCli.ts:126` and `:132`. - What I'd do here is redact all published metadata, including both commit objects, and remove the absolute repo path from static exports. Add assertions for these inputs to `src/server/Ledger.test.ts:618`. The current test checks secrets in session text only. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Raw Git metadata] --> B[Ledger range] B --> C[HTML artifact] B --> D[Job summary] ``` - **P2: Untrusted session messages can make the static page contact an external server.** See `src/web/code.tsx:186` and `src/web/ActionView.tsx:707`. - An assistant message containing `![image](https://)` becomes an image request when the message renders. Markdown has a custom link renderer, but no image restriction. This exposes the reader’s IP and the URL data, and breaks the promised offline behavior. - The fix is straightforward. Render images as text in static pages and block automatic network loads with a CSP. Add a rendered-page test with this input. `src/server/siteTemplate.test.ts:45` checks only the template shell, so it misses images created from session data. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Session message] --> B[Markdown image] B --> C[External request] ``` I found no verified XSS, shell injection, unsafe write-token checkout, or hook-path regression. Package runtime behavior remains unverified. I used Git reads only and ran no builds or tests. The rollout reader, session matching, push retry, and hook installer already exist in `fda8eda`; these seven commits add packaging, the static page, the action, and documentation.

I should test this by rendering the actual page with the attacker image and asserting the output never contains a raw img tag pointing to an external source. I'm considering whether to server-side render the React component in a node test and checking if the web tests run under the right environment for that. But I'm worried ActionView might call localStorage inside a useState initializer, which would break in node—so I should grep for localStorage usage in ActionView first. P1 is committed. Next I'll write a test for P2: server-side render the static `LedgerPage` with an assistant message containing a remote image markdown link, and assert no remote `` is produced—checking what the components touch during render.

I realize client.ts eagerly evaluates `location.origin` at module import time, which would throw ReferenceError in Node since `location` isn't defined — so I'll need to stub globals like `location` with vitest's `vi.stubGlobal` before importing, rather than trying to run a real headless browser for SSR testing.

I need to use `vi.hoisted` to set up the global `location` stub before static imports run, since static imports get hoisted above regular statements. entries.text:
I'm noticing the worktree path also shows up in command outputs like `pwd` within session data, and possibly in file change paths too — so scrubbing just the repo field might not be enough. The existing redaction logic rewrites home directories to `~`, so I should check whether that same approach covers these other absolute path occurrences.

I'll encode the repo path as a JSON-escaped string and replace it with "." before the home directory substitution, since repo paths are longer and more specific. I need to handle boundary cases carefully using a regex with a negative lookahead so a path like "/x/backend" doesn't accidentally match inside "/x/backend-old".

For testing, I'll check that the Ledger test correctly excludes the repo path from entries, then add a core test asserting that an action output containing a sensitive path like "<path>:1" doesn't leak "private-client" after redaction, implementing the fix once that test fails as expected.



The session output includes a `pwd` result that still leaks the client name via the repo path, so I'll update `publicRange` to also replace the repo root with `.`. Testing this change now.
